perplexity.description:
Too Posh To Mosh, Too Good To Last! is a 1987 mini-album by the British rock band Little Angels, originally released under the title Too Posh To Mosh. The album showcases the band's early rock style, characterized by energetic guitar-driven tracks and a raw, melodic approach typical of late 1980s British rock. It captures the formative sound of Little Angels before their full-length studio albums, blending hard rock with accessible hooks and dynamic vocals by Toby Jepson.

This release holds a significant place in Little Angels' discography as their debut recording, laying the groundwork for their subsequent commercial success. The band later expanded on this foundation with full albums like Don't Prey for Me (1989) and Jam (1993), the latter reaching number one on the UK charts. Although Too Posh To Mosh was initially a mini-album, it was reissued in 1994 as Too Posh To Mosh, Too Good To Last! with additional tracks, reflecting its enduring appeal.

Critically, the album was well-received for its energetic performances and solid songwriting, helping establish Little Angels as a notable act in the UK rock scene of the late 1980s. Commercially, the original mini-album contributed to building the band's fanbase, setting the stage for their later chart successes. The 1994 reissue reached number 18 on the UK Albums Chart, underscoring the lasting interest in this early work.
